title: NDP 2026: T-Minus 3 Weeks
description: The NDP committee just approved a brand new parade segment and they want a companion app feature for 40,000 attendees. You have 3 weeks to ship it.
storyContext: 2am. Phone buzzes. The NDP committee just approved a last-minute parade segment and wants a companion app feature for 40,000 people in three weeks. Your team lead's message: "We ship this or we don't ship at all."

software-engineer.title: Plan the Parade App Feature
software-engineer.instruction: Spectators will point their phones at parade floats to see fun facts. Arrange the build steps in the right order.
software-engineer.hint: What if two teams build the same thing without coordinating? When should you test the riskiest part?

items.label: Write a shared plan so teams can build different parts without clashing
Quick test: can the phone camera actually recognise the floats?
Set up the system that sends float info to phones
Test the new feature inside the existing NDP app
Simulate 40,000 people using it at once

data-scientist.title: Forecast App Downloads
data-scientist.instruction: Marketing needs next week's download estimate to prepare capacity. The graph shows the last four weeks. Where does it land next?
data-scientist.hint: The climb is accelerating — each week jumps more than the last. By how much is that jump growing?

cloud-engineer.title: Pick a Hosting Plan
cloud-engineer.instruction: The app must handle 40,000 people on NDP day without costing a fortune the other 364 days. Which approach?
cloud-engineer.hint: One loud day, 364 quiet ones. Think about what matters most — saving money, guaranteed reliability, or raw speed.

options.label: Costs nothing when idle, scales up automatically on the day. First users each hour may wait 2 extra seconds while it wakes up.
Book a fixed set of machines plus extra for NDP day. Reliable, but you pay even when idle.
Spread the app across locations all over Singapore for instant loading. Great for content, but the float scanner may lag.
Partner with a local provider already running government services. Reliable and local, but less flexibility.
